17201.notes: Illinois tax-lien (certificate) county. Winnebago County Treasurer sells unpaid taxes (not the property) at a live reverse auction — bidding from 9% per six months down toward 0%. No phone/internet bids. Annual sale typically mid-to-late November (e.g. Nov 19, 2024 cycle documented). After sale, owner redeems through County Clerk (generally up to 3 years; shorter for vacant/commercial categories under 35 ILCS 200). Unsold liens go to County Trustee; Region 1 Planning Council sells trustee parcels online (min bid often $1,000).

auctionPlatform.label: Winnebago County Treasurer — Tax Sale

17201.auctionFrequency: Annual, typically November. Confirm exact date with Treasurer before registering.
17201.depositRules: Live in-person only; registration and payment rules set by Treasurer for each sale year (similar IL counties require W-9, registration deposit, and funds for full tax amounts won). Contact Treasurer for current registration packet. Redemptions handled by County Clerk after sale.

clerkOfCourt.label: Winnebago County Clerk (tax redemptions)

propertyAppraiser.label: Winnebago County Supervisor of Assessments / WinGIS

17201.survivingLiens: Certificate is a lien on unpaid taxes only. Other liens remain until tax deed process. Federal liens can survive. Interest accrues at winning bid rate every 6 months until redemption or deed.
17201.quietTitle: After tax deed issues, quiet title is commonly required for insurable Illinois tax title.

53035.notes: Washington tax-foreclosure (deed) county — not a tax-lien state. Kitsap County Treasurer begins foreclosure when a tax year is three years late (RCW 84.64). Real property tax foreclosure auction scheduled January 26, 2027 on PublicSurplus.com; last day to redeem January 25, 2027. Treasurer’s deed AS IS without warranty. Separate MH distraint (Nov) and tax-title inventory for unsold parcels. Title companies may wait years to insure.

auctionPlatform.label: Public Surplus — Kitsap County tax foreclosure

53035.auctionFrequency: One primary real-property tax foreclosure auction per year (2027: Jan 26). MH distraint annually in November; tax-title sales as inventory warrants.
53035.depositRules: Register and deposit per Public Surplus / Kitsap sale terms for the cycle (historically Bid4Assets used a single ~$2,500 deposit + $35 fee — confirm current Public Surplus requirements). Certified funds for redemptions (no personal checks).

clerkOfCourt.label: Kitsap County Auditor (recording) / Superior Court

53035.survivingLiens: Most liens extinguished by tax foreclosure, but county makes no guarantees prior lienholders will honor extinguishment; IRS liens subject to 120-day redemption; utility/other easements ≥3 years unaffected; community association covenants and some special assessments may remain.
53035.quietTitle: Some title companies will not insure for up to ten years from tax foreclosure sale date — policies vary; quiet title or long seasoning often needed for financing.

22103.notes: Louisiana tax-lien (ad valorem) parish. St. Tammany Parish Sheriff’s Office sells tax liens (not free-and-clear deeds) at annual online auction on Zeus Auction (SRI). 2025 tax-year sale scheduled July 29, 2026, 8:00 a.m.–4:00 p.m. CT at zeusauction.com; registration opens ~July 1. List of ~2,000 delinquencies advertised in St. Tammany Farmer and on STPSO site. Owners have a three-year redemption period after sale. Separate Civil Division sheriff sales (mortgage/writ) at public.stpso.com are a different product.

auctionPlatform.label: Zeus Auction — St. Tammany Parish tax lien sale

22103.auctionFrequency: Annual (2026: July 29 for 2025 taxes). Delinquent list published mid-July before auction.
22103.depositRules: Create Zeus account and register for St. Tammany sale; payments typically ACH from registered account after sale per SRI/Zeus rules. Property owners must pay before sale cutoff (online payments often close days before auction). Confirm current deposit/ACH requirements on Zeus and secure.stpsopayments.com notices.

clerkOfCourt.label: St. Tammany Parish Clerk of Court (records)

22103.survivingLiens: Tax sale conveys a lien/certificate interest subject to three-year redemption — not immediate free title. Other mortgages/liens may remain until post-redemption quiet title/monition process. Federal liens can survive.
22103.quietTitle: After redemption period, Louisiana monition/quiet-title style proceedings are typically required for marketable title on tax-sale property.

49057.notes: Utah tax-deed county. Weber County Clerk/Auditor auctions real property delinquent four years from final payment deadline (five years including sale year) at annual public outcry sale — typically Thursday before Memorial Day. 2026 sale: May 21, 2026, 10:00 a.m., Weber Center Commission Chambers, 2380 Washington Blvd, Ogden. Registration 9:00 a.m. Minimum bid = taxes, interest, penalty, and administrative costs. Tax deed (not warranty); buyer beware. Unsold parcels may strike off to county.

auctionPlatform.label: Weber County Clerk/Auditor — Tax Sale

49057.auctionFrequency: Annual late May (2026: May 21). Preliminary lists from February of sale year; published ~4 weeks before in Standard Examiner and online.
49057.depositRules: Register morning of sale with Bidder Registration Form; appear in person for bidder number. Full payment in cash or bank-certified funds (no financing). Deposits/deadlines vary by sale amount per bidder packet. Tax deed mailed within ~30 days after County Commission ratification.

clerkOfCourt.label: Weber County Clerk/Auditor / Recorder-Surveyor

49057.survivingLiens: Tax deed is not a warranty deed; county makes no guarantees of title, access, or condition. Federal liens, HOA, easements, and unjoined interests require independent search. Excess funds typically for prior owner; unclaimed to State Treasurer.
49057.quietTitle: Practically required for insurable title after Utah tax deed.

42041.notes: Pennsylvania Tax Claim Bureau county (Real Estate Tax Sale Law of 1947). Cumberland County Tax Claim Bureau conducts Upset Tax Sale (first-round auction of liens/claims) then Judicial Sale for remaining inventory. Upset sale online via Bid4Assets; next tentatively September 18, 2026 (listing mid-July 2026). Upset sales start at taxes + costs; many liens/judgments may survive Upset. Judicial sale aims for freer title after court process. GIS tax-sale property viewer at gis.ccpa.net/taxsales/.

auctionPlatform.label: Cumberland County Tax Claim Bureau — Upset Sale (Bid4Assets)

42041.auctionFrequency: Upset typically September annually (2026 tentative Sept 18). Judicial sales as needed for unsold parcels. Register individual/entity forms on Bureau site.
42041.depositRules: Bid4Assets deposit historically ~$500 + $35 processing for Cumberland Upset cycles — confirm current storefront. Full payment by Bid4Assets settlement deadline after auction. Follow Upset Terms PDF for 2026 cycle.

55009.notes: Wisconsin tax-deed (in rem foreclosure) then county disposition county — not an investor tax-lien certificate auction. After statutory in rem foreclosure, Brown County Treasurer takes tax deed and disposes of county-owned tax-delinquent real estate (historically online via Wisconsin Surplus / bid.wisconsinsurplus.com and related channels). Separate Sheriff sales (2nd & 4th Wednesdays, Target Room, 2684 Development Dr, Green Bay) are primarily mortgage/judgment sales, not the tax-deed pipeline. County budget notes reference updated foreclosure/sales processes post-Supreme Court excess-proceeds rulings. Properties AS IS quitclaim-style.
55009.auctionFormat: Online / OTC as inventory warrants (tax deed); Sheriff sales separate

auctionPlatform.label: Brown County Treasurer — tax-delinquent / county property disposition

55009.auctionFrequency: As tax-deed inventory is ready (not a fixed monthly retail auction). Sheriff foreclosure sales 2nd & 4th Wednesdays — different product. Contact Treasurer for current tax-deed list.
55009.depositRules: Per sale notice when parcels are listed (online surplus auctions typically require registration and deposit/earnest money; full certified funds at closing). Confirm with BC_Treasurer@co.brown.wi.us / (920) 448-4074 before bidding.

clerkOfCourt.label: Brown County Register of Deeds / Clerk of Courts

55009.survivingLiens: In rem tax deed process aims to clear pre-foreclosure tax and many junior interests, but federal liens, environmental issues, access, and post-deed assessments can remain. County disclaims warranties and buildability.
55009.quietTitle: Title companies frequently require quiet title or extended seasoning on Wisconsin tax-deed conveyances before insuring free-and-clear marketable title.

10005.notes: Delaware monition (tax) and mortgage sheriff-sale county. Sussex County Sheriff conducts sales third Tuesday monthly at 9:30 a.m. (Goods & Chattels excepted). Tax/monition sales: 100% of purchase money due same day by 3:00 p.m. in cash, certified check, or cashier’s check payable to Sheriff of Sussex County; buyer also pays share of state and county realty transfer taxes and deed costs. Buyer beware — research parcel thoroughly; ownership change only after proper deed recording. Listings on salesweb.civilview.com (countyId=12). Confirmation typically first Friday after third Monday of following month.

auctionPlatform.label: Sussex County Sheriff Sales / CivilView SalesWeb

10005.auctionFrequency: Third Tuesday of every month at 9:30 a.m. (weather postponements reschedule). Mix of mortgage and monition (tax) parcels — read each listing.
10005.depositRules: Monition/tax sales: entire bid (100%) due by 3:00 p.m. sale day — cash, certified check, or cashier’s check only. Plus buyer’s share of 2.5% DE transfer tax and 1.5% Sussex County realty tax (split seller/purchaser per notice) and deed costs. Make checks payable to Sheriff of Sussex County.

taxCollector.label: Sussex County Finance / Department of Finance (taxes) & Sheriff (sales)

clerkOfCourt.label: Sussex County Recorder of Deeds / Superior Court

10005.survivingLiens: Monition tax sales transfer the tax parcel interest subject to statutory process; federal liens and some interests can survive. Mortgage sheriff sales differ. County materials stress full independent research — no warranty of title or condition.
10005.quietTitle: Often needed for marketable/insurable title after monition tax purchase; confirmation and deed recording steps must be completed first.

48309.notes: Texas tax-deed (constable/tax foreclosure) county. McLennan County Tax Office states all McLennan tax sales are conducted online through GovEase (register at liveauctions.govease.com). Outside counsel McCreary Veselka Bragg & Allen (MVBA) posts monthly tax-sale calendars for Waco/McLennan. Statutory first-Tuesday pattern under Texas law; opening bid generally taxes, penalties, interest, and costs. Post-sale redemption rights apply (generally 2 years for homestead/agricultural; 6 months otherwise — confirm current Tax Code). Buyer beware; HOA/POA liens can survive if not properly joined.

auctionPlatform.label: GovEase — McLennan County tax sales

48309.auctionFrequency: Periodic first-Tuesday-style online sales when inventory is ready (often every other month historically; confirm MVBA monthly calendar and county Tax Office).
48309.depositRules: Pre-register on GovEase by published deadline (e.g. noon CDT day before or as posted). Deposit and final payment per GovEase/McLennan sale terms (certified funds/ACH as platform requires). Training under GovEase Help/Bidder Training.

clerkOfCourt.label: McLennan County Clerk (real property records)

48309.survivingLiens: HOA/POA liens can survive a Texas tax sale if association recorded lien and was not properly joined/notified. Federal tax liens survive (IRS rights). Post-judgment taxes and unjoined municipal liens may remain — search deed records before bidding.
48309.quietTitle: Not legally mandatory, but title companies generally require completed quiet title before insuring because of statutory redemption rights and possible un-joined lienholders.

16027.notes: Idaho tax-deed county — not a tax-lien certificate state. Canyon County takes tax deed on properties delinquent more than three years, holds a tax-deed hearing (e.g. Nov 5 cycle noted on treasurer page), then live public auction of the county’s interest. Auction is in-person only (Commissioners’ Meeting Room pattern). High bidder pays certified funds day of auction; county conveys by quitclaim deed without warranty. Prior owners may redeem until the property is offered at auction. Excess proceeds (after valid claims) go to Idaho State Treasurer unclaimed funds (SB 1347a).

auctionPlatform.label: Canyon County Treasurer — Tax Deed Auction

16027.auctionFrequency: When inventory exists after tax-deed hearing (notice in Idaho Press ~2 weeks prior and on county main page). Not a fixed monthly retail calendar — monitor Treasurer tax-deed page.
16027.depositRules: Must be present to bid. Highest bidder obligated to purchase at bid price and tender certified funds same day. Board may reject any/all bids. Recording and research costs are buyer’s responsibility.

clerkOfCourt.label: Canyon County Recorder / Clerk

16027.survivingLiens: Quitclaim of county’s interest only — not guaranteed clear title. Many parcels are non-viable or landlocked; research by legal description. Federal liens, easements, and access issues require independent search. County does not guarantee accessibility or usability.
16027.quietTitle: Practically required for marketable/insurable title after Idaho tax-deed quitclaim.
